Population increased in Croydon

The estimated population of Croydon in 2024 was 409,342 usual residents, a rise of 1.8% since 2023.

This meant that Croydon's rate of population change placed it among the 20 percent fastest growing local authority districts in England and Wales.

In the period from mid-2021 to mid-2024, the population estimate of Croydon increased by 4.8%.

Over this slightly longer period, Croydon was also among the areas that had a broadly average population increase, of local authority districts in England and Wales.

Age profile of Croydon

The average (median) age fell to 37.5 years between 2023 and 2024.

You can see how the age profile of Croydon has changed since 2011 in the population pyramid below.

sections.content:
Croydon is an area that is classed as urban in nature according to the 2021 Census Rural Urban Classification.

By age category, Croydon's population of 409,342 usual residents was made up of:

  • 82,949 people aged 0 to 15 years, (20.3%)
  • 269,659 people aged 16 to 64 years, (65.9%)
  • 56,734 people aged 65 years and over, (13.9%)

    • Compared with England and Wales as a whole, Croydon has a lower proportion of people aged 65 years and over (13.9% compared with 18.9% for England and Wales).

Contributors to population change

We look at different flows of people into and out of areas and births and deaths to see what is driving population change in each area.

In Croydon, the largest contribution to population change in the year to mid-2024 was from net international migration.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Croydon
sections.subtitle: How the population changed, by component

sections.content:
We estimate that, for Croydon, between 2023 and 2024:

  • More births than deaths increased the population of 2,213 people (0.6%). In total, there were 5,001 births and 2,788 deaths in Croydon.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other areas in the UK) led to a fall in the population of 3,785 (-0.9%). There were 31,451 people entering the area and 35,236 people leaving the area.
  • Net international migration led to an increase in Croydon's population of 8,698 (2.2%) as a result of 11,898 people entering the area and 3,200 people leaving the area.
  • Other change (which includes changes to armed forces personnel and prisoners) for Croydon was less than 0.1%.

Revisions to 2023 population estimates

We regularly revise our initial population estimates as we get more data and methods improve.

Our revised estimate for the population of Croydon in mid-2023 is 402,217.

Within this, international migration was revised upwards by 4,573 people and internal migration estimates were revised downwards by 97 people.

Overall, there was an revision upwards of 4,476 people.
